 return sum(exp(-1j*a[p])/(e[(p-1)%3]*e[(p+1)%3]) for p in range(3))

strengths: The formulation addresses an important scientific-vision problem: recovering explicit cell surfaces without annotated training data. Combining surface-supported fluorophore distributions with differentiable optical convolution is well motivated and potentially useful for quantitative biological analysis.

The custom CUDA implementation of mesh Fourier transforms and vertex gradients is a concrete technical contribution. Figure 6 reports substantial acceleration, and the spectral cutoff exploits the microscope’s limited frequency response sensibly.

Experiments cover several synthetic geometries and mouse, ascidian, and worm embryos across imaging modalities. On 15 organoid volumes, Figure 9 reports better image reconstruction than DM3D, including MSE of 0.0020 versus 0.0125 and SSIM of 0.8021 versus 0.7101.

The pipeline diagrams communicate the approach clearly. The manuscript credits data contributors, cites a versioned implementation archive, and acknowledges limitations of Gaussian and translation-invariant PSFs.
weaknesses: The central claim of accurate cell geometry lacks independent quantitative validation. Sections 6.1–6.3 primarily measure rendered-image agreement, even when synthetic ground-truth meshes are available. The DM3D comparison also uses the proposed renderer and inferred PSF, with the baseline’s PSF-fitting protocol insufficiently specified. Better image agreement does not necessarily imply better boundaries, curvature, or cell volumes. Surface-distance measurements and independently annotated biological examples would substantially strengthen the scientific case.

Joint shape–PSF inference is insufficiently evaluated. Section 6.1 uses the generating Gaussian PSF during inference to isolate shape reconstruction, while the real-data examples provide no PSF recovery errors or independent optical calibration. Consequently, the experiments do not establish whether estimated blur is physically meaningful or compensates for geometric and fluorescence-model errors. Controlled unknown-PSF experiments and fixed-versus-optimized PSF comparisons are needed.

The robustness and regularization claims exceed the supporting evidence. Although no explicit shape penalty is added to the objective, Section 5.1 applies substantial Laplacian gradient smoothing with lambda = 50. Its contribution is not separated from that of the optical model. Initialization and noise experiments concern one reference shape, with an unspecified noise distribution and no variability estimates; embryo initialization additionally assumes the correct cell count. These results support a narrower robustness claim.

Several mathematical statements require correction. Under the stated Fourier convention, the Gaussian transform following Eq. (2) should contain the covariance matrix rather than its inverse. The edge-projection arguments introduced before Eq. (11) cannot reproduce the translation-dependent transform in Eq. (8), and Eq. (11)’s exponential sign disagrees with its stated limits in Eq. (12). These may be transcription errors rather than implementation failures, but corrected formulas and numerical gradient checks are necessary to make the technical account reliable.

Practical scalability remains unclear. Figure 6 benchmarks individual rendering operations, whereas reconstruction requires 1,000–10,000 optimization steps and full-frequency evaluations for PSF updates. Representative end-to-end times, peak memory, and the accuracy–speed tradeoff of spectral truncation are missing. Learning rates, the shape/PSF update schedule, and enforcement of valid covariance matrices also need clearer specification despite the implementation link.

Originality is clearest in the integration and implementation. The stronger 'new paradigm' and 'first-of-its-kind' framing needs more precise differentiation from the cited deconvolving active contours [31, 64] and spectral geometric processing [37]. The manuscript does not adequately isolate which advances over these antecedents drive its empirical benefits.
